note: In this family a forename is inherited property. It travels through daughters as reliably as a surname travels through sons, it survives a change of surname, and it survives the death of the person it came from. Three times it has also produced an error in this archive, because two people of one name in two generations look exactly alike in an index. AND IT IS EVIDENCE. Read carefully it says which family a child belongs to: OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS runs four generations out of a single marriage and is not a Booysen name at all, and the eldest son of a disputed man is called DAVID SCHALK, which is the third argument on the disputed page for a father this site did not give him.

sets.sub: Five generations, and it does not come from this family at all
sets.kick: The name enters through a step-relation with no blood tie to any Booyzen, and is still being given to children a century and a half later.
who: Anna Catharina Slier's FIRST husband. Not a Booyzen, not a Mountjoy, and no blood relation to either.
His son by her, and godfather at the 1851 Graaff-Reinet font — half-brother to Johanna Catharina Mountjoy.
Named at that font for the godfather standing over it. Generation four of the direct line.
The miner. An eighth child this archive did not know it had until the register turned him up.
Baptised at Indwe, entered “onecht”, his grandmother standing godmother.
And out through a daughter into a third surname.
sets.note: This archive published “Willem Hermanus is a Booyzen name” and withdrew it. Three documents name the first husband three ways — Harmanus Pieterze in 1817, William Pietersen in 1840, Willem Hermanus Pieterzen in 1851 — and the man they name married into the line and died before it started.

sets.sub: Four generations of women, across three surnames
sets.kick: A Barry name that outlives the Barry surname by eighty years.
who: The last Barry of the surname in this line. She married a Booyzen in 1879.
Baptised at Barkly Oost, “named for her mother entire”. She married a Daschner at Indwe.
Her eldest daughter — the third of the name, and the second surname it has crossed.
And back into the Booyzens, on the direct line, the hinge to the Lerena archive.
sets.note: A fifth carries it too: Catharina Mary Sophia Däschner, born at Indwe on 11 March 1909, baptised there that May.

sets.sub: The spine name — five men over a hundred and fifty years
sets.kick: 1788, 1812, 1839, 1904, 1934. Two of them are on the direct line and three are not, and an index cannot tell them apart.
who: Generation six. Died at Brakfontein, district Rustenburg, with nothing to leave.
Generation five. The farmer at Zevenfontein who signed his wife's death notice.
Third child on the 1863 death notice.
Baptised with a Z at Middelburg, a year before the Indwe sheet spelled it with an S.
sets.note: Three of these share one page on this site, because merging them silently would be worse than saying so.

sets.sub: The name that made this archive get something wrong
sets.kick: An uncle and a nephew, both of this name, both connected to an estate filed in 1885.
who: Generation seven — the top of the male line, and the source of the name.
His grandson. Fifth on the 1876 Sterfkennis; died at Vaalbank, district Lichtenburg. THE ESTATE IS HIS.
His great-grandson, seventh on the 1863 death notice. This archive gave him the uncle's estate and a death date to match. Both are withdrawn.
And a third, who died in a concentration camp — of the western Transvaal family this archive spent months insisting was somebody else's.
sets.note: The error is on the corrections page. A year was read off a file number, written into a man's life as a death date, and then cited back as though it were evidence.

sets.n: The Barry names, after the Barrys
sets.sub: Six forenames cross into a family called Daschner
sets.kick: The surname stops in 1859. The names do not stop at all.
who: Kathleen Barry's own name, third generation running.
Margaret Wilhelmina Elizabeth Jeanette van Jaarsveld
The Barry name that also runs down the Pretorius side and reaches Maggie Booyzen in 1926.
For his great-uncle Richard Peter Barry of Manorowen.
For his uncle Henry James Booyzen.
AND GEORGE DOWNING TOO — buried at Brixton, Johannesburg, the year he was born. A second of the name died in 1998.
sets.note: Six of eleven children. When the Cape Rebel roll produces a Richard Peter Barry of Jerpoint, the name is evidence of a family and not of an individual — and this archive still marks that identification unproven.

sets.sub: A dead child's name given again — and the only time this archive can watch it happen
sets.kick: Fourteen months old when she died. Four years later her parents used the name again, and it is still running two generations on.
who: The grandmother. Born in the district of Cradock, died at her own house at Dordrecht.
Baptised at Dordrecht three weeks after she was born, named for her grandmother entire, and dead at fourteen months in Wodehouse.
Baptised at Aberdeen, and given the whole name again. She married Hendrik Stefanus Palm.
And a granddaughter, twenty-four years after the first of the name was buried.
sets.note: Replacement naming — a child who dies young and a later child given the same name — is well attested in these congregations and is exactly how a records-matcher invents one person out of two. Here the dates make it unmistakable: a death in October 1897 and a birth in November 1901. This archive keeps the two apart, and says which is which.

sets.sub: One name, three surnames, no blood tie proved between two of them
sets.kick: It comes out of the London Kolbes and ends up on a Booÿsen born in the year the war began.
who: Carried into the Barrys by the Kolbe marriage of 1850.
And into the Booysens, spelled with a diaeresis, in 1899.
sets.note: Ruben, a Schoeman name, travels the same way into the Barrys — Ruben Jacobus Josuah Barry.

sets.sub: Two daughters, one name, eleven months apart
sets.kick: Not a duplicated record. Two children, two death certificates, two cemeteries.
who: Four days old. Queen Victoria Hospital.
Six hours old, entry 3920, Turf Club Nursing Home. A different hospital and a different cemetery.
sets.note: Born on the same date a year apart, and both named for the same person. This archive checked it precisely because it looked like an indexing error, and it is not one.

sets.n: And it runs the other way too
sets.sub: The van Niekerk names crossing into the Mountjoys
sets.kick: The same habit, observed from a second direction and in a second family — which is what makes it a habit rather than a coincidence.
who: For his mother's father, Jan Dirk Abram Frans van Niekerk of Dordrecht.
And the Booyzen name, into the Mountjoys, twenty-six years after the two families stood at the same font at Barkly Oost.
sets.note: Five of the eight children of Hercules Johannes Mountjoy and Maria Sophia van Niekerk are named for a grandparent or a parent. These come from the Dutch Reformed INDEX and not from the register images, and the person pages say so.

sets.n: And into a family called Keys
sets.sub: The Mountjoy names, crossing a third surname at Dordrecht
sets.kick: The habit again, in a family this archive did not know existed until this afternoon.
who: Married a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. Their children were baptised at Dordrecht, Burgersdorp and Barkly East between 1878 and 1897.
Baptised at Dordrecht — and named for James Jonathan Mountjoy, the retired builder of Barkly East.
Named for Herklaas — Hercules Johannes Mountjoy.
Maria Sophia, which is both a Mountjoy and a van Niekerk name.
And on the other side of the family, a Barry carrying the rebel's forename and the Settler's surname in one.
sets.note: All from the index rather than from register images, and the person pages say so. Three surnames now carry these forenames out of the family that coined them: Daschner, Keys, and van Jaarsveld.

sets.sub: Four generations, out of one marriage, and it is not a Booysen name at all
sets.kick: Yesterday this archive could not account for the forename anywhere in six generations of Booysens. It comes in with one wife, from the district of Cradock, and then will not leave.
who: HER FATHER. Married Anna Catharina Botha at Graaff-Reinet on 8 December 1816 and baptised four children at Cradock. Not a Booysen.
Ockert Johannes Stephanus Olivier the younger
His son, named for him entire.
HIS GRANDSON, by Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier — and the man who signed his own father's death notice in 1908. Confirmed at Rustenburg in 1869 on the same Sunday as his brother.
Named on his father's 1935 Sterfkennis as a minor of seven. FOUR generations on from Cradock.

sets.sub: Three women, three generations, the same two names
sets.kick: The 1900 death notice of one of them names the other two — a grandmother, a mother and a daughter who died a minor, all carrying it.
who: The grandmother, named on the 1900 notice as the deceased's own mother.
Her daughter. Died in a zinc building in Market Street, Pretoria, four days before Lord Roberts entered the town.
Her daughter, squeezed in between the lines of that notice after it had been written, with DIED MINOR against her.

sets.sub: An aunt in 1823, a niece two generations later
sets.kick: The names in the Olivier household run back up the female line, and this archive could not see it until both baptisms were read on the same afternoon.
who: Baptised at Cradock eleven months before her sister Anna Johanna.
Anna Johanna's own daughter, named on her mother's 1891 Sterfkennis and again on her father's 1908 notice, married in community of property to Stephanus Andries Venter.

sets.n: The Boshoff grandparents, and what they prove
sets.sub: Two children out of eleven, called straight after their mother's parents
sets.kick: Worth noticing not for itself but for what it settles: this couple DID name children after grandparents, deliberately — which is why the eldest son's name is evidence in a disputed parentage.
who: Her father, named on her 1890 baptism at Mossel Bay.
Their grandson, named on the 1940 estate.
Her mother, named on the same baptism.
Their granddaughter, who married a Luus. All three of her grandmother's names.
And the ELDEST son is called David Schalk — which is a point in the argument about whose son his father was. See /disputed/.

sets.sub: Two names that come from outside and appear nowhere else here
sets.kick: Most of this archive's names repeat until they are meaningless. These two arrive with an in-law and stop.
who: Eldest of the eight Keys children by Johanna Catharina Mountjoy.
The second Byron. The name comes from the Keys side, not the Mountjoy.
A son of Charlotta Dormehl by her FIRST husband.
A son of the same woman by her SECOND husband. SYBERT crossing between two marriages of one woman.
